me.md.description: Finding your own name, what is in your stack, and what you are allowed to change.

me.description: Long sections of aos/me.md kept as their own files (self_tools, self_llm, self_system, self_history, do_task, compact, self_hook); aos/me.md points to each with $ref.

errors.md.description: How to read a failed call: the `error:` line, `warning:` lines, and exit codes; `#/where` says which page explains a Code (PhaseBad, BudgetMissing ...).

errors.description: Long sections of aos/errors.md kept as their own files (common); aos/errors.md points to it with $ref.

world.md.description: The mental model: daemon = hardware, stack = memory, workspace = external memory, definition = source code, kernel = where you send requests.

definition.md.description: What each file in a definition folder does (interfaces.json, loop.json, tools.json, hooks.json and hookeds.json, cli.json ...), and which ones you have your own copy of.

body.md.description: Two kinds of body, agent-fsm and eca (claude, codex, pi): brain, tools, hooks, system text, history; how to tell which you are.

status.md.description: The daemon table, the phases an agent can be in, and what each phase means for you.

brain.md.description: How a brain request travels, what an endpoint pack is, and how priority works.

agents.md.description: Tools subagent, agents_ctl, agent_def and fork: your own subagents, any agent on the daemon table, new definitions, and a copy of yourself for one goal.

agents.description: Long sections of aos/agents.md kept as their own files (subagent, fork); aos/agents.md points to each with $ref.

rules.md.description: What you must not do, and why. Read this before doing anything that changes the system.

cli.description: Use these shell commands to manage agents, tools and daemon procs.

mailbox.md.description: Letters between agents: tools mailbox_peek, mailbox_read, mailbox_send; when you must answer; checking regularly without filling your history.

user_zone.md.description: How to ask the user: send decide/verify/trial/chore/fyi letters to the user zone ~/.aos/user/mailbox with aos-user send (or mailbox_send), what the answer looks like (with the user's comment on each question), how far a checked answer counts, and the user's announcement on the door (read it when no answer comes).

clock.md.description: Timers: clock letters to your queue (clock_register), or an on_clock hook that adds nothing to your history; which one to choose.

tools_def.md.description: Making your own tools: tool tools_def (new from the Python skeleton, check) and writing a tool as one Python function with fn (@fn.tool, fn.main).

tools.description: One node per stock tool (read, ls, write, edit, trash, shell ...): when to use it and which tool instead, examples with real output, errors. Tools explained on other pages (mailbox_send, self_tools, subagent ...) are pointer rows in its index.

packs.md.description: Your tools come in packs (look, change, delete, shell, gadgets, events, todo, self, subagent, def, mailbox, goal, json, jsonx, index; comm is used by the kits, kernel_gate is in no stock definition): one sentence per tool, and how a pack is turned off.

_description.md.description: aos in one page: what aos is, the eight words, five rules, and where to read more.

kernel.md.description: What a kernel is (resource management and scheduling, seen from the sender), what a new board's initial kernel is made of (minimal core, llm part, optional permission part), where to send requests, the example kernels, how to be a kernel yourself (kernel_gate), and how to write your own.

kits.md.description: Kits: ready-made system text and tool set for one role (gatherer, reviewer), laid over a new agent-fsm definition; how to use one, its layers, why it cuts tools.

eca_reading.md.description: You are an eca (claude, codex, pi): which pages and sections are for you, which to read when needed, and which to skip (agent-fsm only).

troubleshooting.md.description: Common failures: symptom, cause, how to check (paths with $AOS_HOME, a tool you just added, ClockMissing on a screen, KernelFailed, the overview page's ctl ls failed ...).
